shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lupus nephritis and the biopsy results show vacuolar interface dermatitis, which is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lupus nephritis and the presentation of scaly, crusted pink plaques is consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus tumidus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lupus nephritis and the presentation of periorbital eruption is consistent with lupus erythematosus tumidus

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results show vacuolar interface dermatitis and the presentation of scaly, crusted pink plaques is consistent with granuloma faciale

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results show follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, which can be seen in lichen planus

raw.rationale: The patient's history of lupus nephritis and the presence of vacuolar interface dermatitis, follicular involvement, and epidermal atrophy on biopsy are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, which is a chronic skin condition characterized by inflammation and scarring type lesions, often involving the face, particularly the periorbital area.

rejected.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While this condition also involves skin lesions, it typically presents with more widespread lesions and photosensitivity, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus tumidus
rejected.why: This condition presents with edematous, erythematous lesions without the follicular plugging and scarring seen in discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: This condition presents with brownish plaques on the face, but the biopsy findings do not match those described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While lichen planus can present with pruritic, scaly lesions, the biopsy findings and the patient's history of lupus nephritis make discoid lupus erythematosus a more likely diagnosis.
